plaintext_source: OMN-17288 and OMN-18024 (Linear, private workspace). OMN-18024's entries are also resolvable from the pre-fix parent of its merge commit at the path:line each entry's notes field names -- the values are public in this repository's history and the operator ruled document-and-accept on history.
readme: Each entry is a salted SHA-256 of a forbidden literal. The plaintext is deliberately
ABSENT: this file ships in PUBLIC repos, and writing the literal here would create the
exact fresh, greppable, current-tree occurrence the gate exists to prevent.
The salt is committed. That makes this obfuscation, not secrecy -- a reader with this
file can brute-force a short slug. It is not trying to be a confidentiality control:
the OMN-17288 values are already public in git history and the operator ruled
document-and-accept on that. The property that matters is FORWARD safety -- the next
entry added here may be a live identifier that has NOT leaked, and this format is safe
for that case where a plaintext denylist would not be.
paste the emitted object here, and record the plaintext in the owning Linear ticket.
